questions.questionHtml:
🔥 GATE 2027 Original: Probability & Statistics - Bayes Theorem

In a test for a rare disease affecting 1 in 1000 people, the test has a false positive rate of 5% (i.e. Probability(Positive | Healthy) = 0.05) and a sensitivity of 99% (i.e. Probability(Positive | Diseased) = 0.99). If a randomly chosen person tests positive, what is the posterior probability (expressed as a percentage, rounded to 1 decimal place) that the person actually has the disease?

💡 Detailed Concept & Solution:
Prior $P(D) = 0.001$, $P(H) = 0.999$.
$P(+ | D) = 0.99$, $P(+ | H) = 0.05$.
By Bayes' Theorem:
$$P(D | +) = \frac{P(+ | D) P(D)}{P(+ | D) P(D) + P(+ | H) P(H)}$$
$$P(D | +) = \frac{0.99 \times 0.001}{(0.99 \times 0.001) + (0.05 \times 0.999)} = \frac{0.00099}{0.00099 + 0.04995} = \frac{0.00099}{0.05094} \approx 0.01943 = 1.9\%$$\.

🔥 GATE 2027 Original: Computer Organization - Pipelining

A 5-stage instruction pipeline has an ideal CPI of 1. Branch instructions constitute 20% of the instruction mix. Conditional branches are resolved in the 3rd stage (causing a 2-cycle penalty on misprediction). A dynamic branch predictor is used with a prediction accuracy of 85%. Assuming no other pipeline stalls, what is the effective CPI of this processor? (Round to 2 decimal places).

💡 Detailed Concept & Solution:
Branch frequency = 0.20.
Misprediction rate $= 1 - 0.85 = 0.15$.
Penalty per mispredicted branch = 2 cycles.

In the context of the pipeline, 'Predict-not-taken' is a method of branch prediction in which the hardware assumes that the next instruction to be executed will be the instruction following the branch instruction in memory. This (possible) next instruction is placed in the pipe and execution begins. If after the branch is finished executing, it is found that we really wanted to take the branch, then the (possible) next instruction that we had been executing is thrown out by the hardware, and we begin executing the correct instruction, the branch target. Consider two different 55-stage pipeline machines (IF ID EX MEM WB).(IF ID EX MEM WB). The first machine MM resolves branches in the IDID stage, uses one branch delay slot, and can fill 80%80% of the delay slots with useful instructions. The second machine NN resolves branches in the EXEX stage and uses a Predict-not-taken scheme. Assume that the cycle times of the machines are identical. Given that 35%35% of the instructions are branches, 25%25% of branches are taken, and that stalls are due to branches alone, what is the Speedup of machine MM over machine NN (up to three decimal places)? (Speedup is the ratio of machine NN running time to machine MM running time.)

Consider an array of nn distinct integers. An array element is a peak if it is greater than its neighbors.
For corner elements, we need to consider only one neighbor. The corner element is peak only when it's greater than its neighbors.
If there are more than one peak item, simply return one of them.

  • Input :[1,5,3,2,4,0]:[1,5,3,2,4,0] Output :4:4
  • Input :[1,2,3,4,5,6]:[1,2,3,4,5,6] Output :6:6
  • Input :[7,6,5,4,3,2]:[7,6,5,4,3,2] Output :7:7

We design a divide-and-conquer algorithm that solves this problem. The incomplete pseudo-code is given below.

  1. findPeak(A, i, j){
  2.     if(i==j) //one element
  3.         return i 
  4.     if(i==j-1) //two elements
  5.         if(A[i]> A[j] ) return i
  6.         else return j
  7.     mid = (i+j)/2
  8.     if (A[mid]> A[mid-1] and A[mid]> A[mid+1]) return mid
  9.     if (A[mid-1]> A[mid])
  10.     //line X
  11.     if (A[mid+1]> A[mid])
  12.     //line Y
